description: Designing data warehouses that answer business questions and mining them for patterns: multidimensional modelling, warehouse implementation, data preprocessing, association analysis, classification and prediction with attention to bias and variance, and clustering, each applied to real datasets. Taught to the depth of a leading data mining course.
modelledOn: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques
Tan, Steinbach, Karpatne and Kumar, Introduction to Data Mining
Kimball and Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit
Witten, Frank, Hall and Pal, Data Mining: Practical Machine Learning Tools and Techniques
outcomes: Design a data warehouse with dimensional models and explain its architecture and ETL processes.
Choose and implement star, snowflake and fact-constellation schemas and OLAP operations.
Implement a warehouse and connect a data mining architecture to it.
Clean, integrate, reduce, transform and discretise data for mining.
Mine frequent itemsets and association rules and evaluate their interestingness.
Build, evaluate and compare classifiers, predictors and clustering methods, and explain bias and variance.

units.title: Data warehousing and modelling
topics: Operational systems versus decision support; the data warehouse definition: subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile
Warehouse architecture: sources, staging, ETL/ELT, the warehouse, data marts, metadata, presentation tools
Dimensional modelling: facts, measures, grain, dimensions, hierarchies; slowly changing dimensions
Requirements gathering with business users: a retail chain, a telecom, a university registry

units.title: Schemas for multidimensional data
topics: Data cubes, dimensions and measures; the lattice of cuboids
Star, snowflake and fact constellation schemas; conformed dimensions; surrogate keys
OLAP operations: roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot; ROLAP, MOLAP, HOLAP
SQL extensions for analytics: GROUP BY CUBE and ROLLUP, window functions, materialised views

units.title: Warehouse implementation and data mining architecture
topics: Building the warehouse in PostgreSQL or a cloud warehouse; loading with ETL tools or Python; indexing (bitmap, join indexes); partitioning
Cube computation and materialisation strategies; query processing and performance
Metadata and data quality management; warehouse operations and refresh
The data mining process (KDD, CRISP-DM); architecture: data sources, warehouse server, mining engine, pattern evaluation, GUI
Tools: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, mlxtend), R, Weka, Orange

units.title: Data preprocessing
topics: Data types and statistics; visualising and summarising data; measuring similarity and dissimilarity
Data cleaning: missing values, noise (binning, regression, outlier detection), inconsistencies
Data integration: entity identification, redundancy and correlation analysis, conflict resolution
Data reduction: sampling, dimensionality reduction (PCA, attribute selection), numerosity reduction, compression
Transformation: normalisation (min-max, z-score), discretisation (binning, entropy-based), concept hierarchies

units.title: Association analysis
topics: Market basket analysis; itemsets, support, confidence, lift, conviction
Apriori: candidate generation, pruning, rule generation; efficiency improvements
FP-growth and the FP-tree; closed and maximal itemsets
Multilevel and multidimensional associations; sequential patterns in brief
Interestingness measures and avoiding misleading rules; mining a supermarket or mobile-money dataset

units.title: Classification and prediction; bias and variance
topics: Decision tree induction (ID3, C4.5, CART), attribute selection measures, pruning; rule-based classifiers
Bayesian classification, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machines, neural networks, ensembles (bagging, boosting, random forests)
Prediction: linear and nonlinear regression
Evaluation: holdout, cross-validation, bootstrap; confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, ROC; comparing classifiers statistically
Bias and variance: decomposition, learning curves, underfitting and overfitting, model complexity, regularisation
Class imbalance and cost-sensitive learning

units.title: Clustering analysis
topics: Clustering requirements and types of data; partitioning methods: k-means, k-medoids (PAM, CLARA)
Hierarchical methods: agglomerative, divisive, BIRCH; density-based: DBSCAN, OPTICS; grid-based: STING
Model-based clustering (EM); clustering high-dimensional data; constraint-based clustering
Evaluating clusters: silhouette, cohesion and separation; outlier analysis

units.title: Applications, trends and capstone
topics: Mining text, web, time series and graphs in brief; recommender systems
Privacy-preserving data mining and the ethics of profiling; the Data Protection Act
Capstone: build a warehouse for a dataset, run OLAP reports and apply association, classification and clustering with a written interpretation
Presentation to a non-technical audience

schedule.title: Decision support and warehouse architecture
schedule.exercise: Contrast an operational mobile-money transaction system with a decision-support warehouse for the same company, and draw the flow from sources through staging and ETL to data marts.

tasks.title: Run the same sales question against a provided operational schema and a warehouse table, and compare query complexity and result
Draw an architecture diagram with three source systems, a staging area, an ETL step, a warehouse and two data marts, labelling metadata stores
Write staging-to-warehouse SQL that loads cleaned orders, rejects rows violating three listed rules into an error table, and reconcile row counts

schedule.title: Dimensional modelling and requirements
schedule.exercise: Interview a classmate playing a supermarket manager, record five business questions, and turn them into a declared grain, a list of facts and dimensions, and a bus matrix.

tasks.title: Create a sales fact table at the grain of one product per receipt line with date, product and store dimensions, and load ten rows
Implement a Type 2 slowly changing customer dimension, apply two address changes, and query the customer history as of a chosen date
Run a requirements interview scenario with a telecom business user, choose the right grain and measures, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Cubes, schemas and OLAP queries
schedule.exercise: For a three-dimension sales cube, list all cuboids in the lattice, then show by hand which roll-up, drill-down, slice and dice moves answer four given questions.

tasks.title: Write queries performing a roll-up from month to year and a slice on one region over a provided star schema and check the totals
Use GROUP BY ROLLUP and CUBE on a sales star schema to produce subtotals, and check the grand total equals the base table sum
Convert a star schema to a snowflake by normalising the product dimension, compare query plans for the same report, and explain the trade-off

schedule.title: Building and tuning the warehouse
schedule.exercise: Propose a monthly refresh and partitioning strategy for a 500 million row sales fact table, with the materialised cuboids you would precompute and the data quality checks run at each load.

tasks.title: Load a provided CSV into a staging table with Python, transform it into a dimension table, and verify the final row count
Create a materialised summary table for monthly sales by region and compare the query plan and cost with and without it
Write data quality checks for completeness, duplicates and referential integrity on a warehouse load and identify planted defects in a given batch

schedule.title: The data mining process and tools
schedule.exercise: Map a customer churn project for a Ghanaian telecom to the six CRISP-DM phases, listing the deliverable and one risk at each phase.

tasks.title: Load a provided dataset with pandas, print summary statistics and class counts, and identify two columns that will need cleaning
Draw a process diagram of the KDD steps for a loan-default mining project and annotate the tool used at each step
Build a scikit-learn pipeline chaining imputation, scaling and a classifier, and compare it with the same steps coded by hand on one dataset

schedule.title: Understanding, cleaning and integrating data
schedule.exercise: Inspect a messy health-facility visits table, list every quality problem found, choose a fix for each missing value, outlier and inconsistency, and justify the choices.

tasks.title: Compute the mean, median and standard deviation of each numeric column in a dataset and draw a box plot to spot outliers
Impute missing values three ways (mean, median, nearest neighbour) on a dataset and compare the effect on the column's distribution
Merge two customer tables with inconsistent names and IDs using entity matching, then test attribute redundancy with a correlation matrix

schedule.title: Data reduction and transformation
schedule.exercise: Normalise a small income and age table by min-max and z-score by hand, then explain when each is preferable and what discretisation would lose.

tasks.title: Apply min-max and z-score normalisation to a numeric column and confirm the new range and mean and standard deviation
Run PCA on a 10-attribute dataset, choose components explaining 90 percent of variance, and plot the first two components coloured by class
Discretise a numeric attribute with equal-width, equal-frequency and entropy-based binning, then compare downstream decision tree accuracy for each

schedule.title: Frequent itemsets and association rules
schedule.exercise: For a 10-transaction basket table, hand-run two passes of Apriori with minimum support 30 percent, and compute support, confidence and lift for two derived rules.

tasks.title: Compute support, confidence and lift for three given rules from a small basket table and say which is most interesting
Implement Apriori with candidate pruning on a basket dataset and report how many candidates the pruning step removes at each level
Build an FP-tree for a given dataset, mine it, and compare runtime and itemsets found against Apriori at three support thresholds

schedule.title: Association rules in practice
schedule.exercise: Take five association rules mined from a mobile-money dataset, classify each as useful, trivial or misleading, and explain with lift and a plausible lurking variable.

tasks.title: Mine rules from a supermarket dataset with mlxtend at minimum support 5 percent and list the top five by lift
Mine rules at the product category level and at the item level, and compare which rules appear only at the higher level
Identify a misleading high-confidence rule in a given dataset using lift and conviction, and show with a contingency table why it is spurious

schedule.title: Classification and prediction
schedule.exercise: Compute the information gain and Gini index for two candidate splits on a small loan table, choose the root, and describe how pruning and ensembles reduce overfitting.

tasks.title: Grow a decision tree on the provided weather dataset in the visualiser and note the attribute chosen at each level and its gain
Train naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbours and a random forest on one dataset and compare their test accuracy in a single table
Fit linear, polynomial and decision tree regression to housing prices in Accra and compare their errors on held-out data

schedule.title: Evaluating and tuning models
schedule.exercise: From a given confusion matrix for a fraud detector, compute accuracy, precision, recall and F1, and explain why accuracy misleads when fraud is 1 percent of cases.

tasks.title: Compute a confusion matrix, precision, recall and F1 from provided predictions and draw the ROC curve for the classifier scores
Plot learning curves for a decision tree at depths 1 to 12, locate the overfitting point, and add regularisation to improve validation score
Handle a 1 percent fraud dataset with class weights and resampling, and compare recall and precision under 5-fold cross-validation for each approach

schedule.title: Cluster analysis
schedule.exercise: Run two iterations of k-means by hand on eight 2D points with k = 2, then explain when DBSCAN would succeed where k-means fails.

tasks.title: Cluster a provided 2D customer dataset with k-means for k = 3 and plot the points coloured by cluster with centroids marked
Build a dendrogram for 12 points with single and average linkage, cut at three clusters, and compare the memberships
Compare k-means and DBSCAN on a crescent-shaped dataset using silhouette scores, tune eps and min points, and flag outliers

schedule.title: Advanced topics, ethics and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present a five-minute summary of the capstone findings to a non-technical manager, with two charts, one recommendation and one limitation, and a note on data protection obligations.

tasks.title: Build a user-based recommender for a small ratings table and list the top three recommendations for one chosen user
Work through a profiling case where a lender mines customer data, decide what to use and withhold, and score against the data protection rubric
Build a star schema for a provided retail dataset, run three OLAP reports, then mine one association rule set and one classifier on it
